content:
morgan: Heads up — CI started failing to create pods in the gpu-pool namespace after yesterday's RBAC refactor. deploys error with 403. Anyone seen this?

alex: I saw the alerts. The refactor removed a broad ClusterRoleBinding we relied on. CI used to have a cluster wide binding. We need a least-priv Role for the deployer SA in gpu-pool.

sasha: Confirmed in audit: multiple forbidden events for system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer -> kubernetes api returned 403 for create on pods in namespace gpu-pool. Audit excerpt: ```{ "verb": "create", "user": "system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer", "resource": "pods", "namespace": "gpu-pool", "responseStatus": 403 }```

morgan: Oof. Is immediate fix to re-add the old ClusterRoleBinding? I want minimum blast radius.

alex: Don’t re-add cluster-admin. Quick safe fix is a namespaced Role + RoleBinding giving create/get/list/watch/update/patch on pods, pods/exec, and pods/log in gpu-pool. We should scope to serviceaccount ci:deployer. Example Role YAML: ```apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: ci-deployer-gpu-pool
  namespace: gpu-pool
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","pods/exec","pods/log"]
  verbs: ["create","get","list","watch","update","patch"]```

sasha: That matches what logs show we need. Also we have to check CRDs used by the runtime (gpupool CR?) — if the deployer needs to patch GPUPool custom resource we must add that permission. Audit shows a couple of patch requests to customresourcedefinitions failing.

deploy-bot: deploy failed: error creating pod: pods "inference-123" is forbidden: user "system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer" cannot create resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "gpu-pool"

security-bot: Note on KMS: some infra changes also touched secret encryption settings. If CI needs to mount secrets that are KMS-encrypted we must ensure the SA has access to the KMS key via IAM role (for cloud provider). Rolling RBAC alone won't fix KMS-permission denies. Check KMS policy for the CI IAM role.

alex: Good catch — I checked: kube secrets are using envelope encryption with GCP KMS key redwood-infra-master. CI uses a GKE Workload Identity service account mapped to google-sa-ci; google-sa-ci needs 'cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' on the key. Not present for the new google-sa. I'll open a permit PR.

morgan: Can we do a short-term remediation: 1) apply namespaced Role + RoleBinding 2) add KMS IAM on google-sa-ci 3) confirm audit events go away

sasha: Yes. Also let's enable an auditSink to forward forbidden events to splunk so we can alert on regressions. Small policy to catch 403s on create/patch for gpu-pool ns.

alex: I'll push the Role/RoleBinding YAML and a small terraform change to attach kms role. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/428 (WIP).

morgan: Awesome. Once applied, someone from CI team should run the deploy job and paste the logs.

deploy-bot: retry triggered by morgan: starting deploy... 

deploy-bot: deploy success: pod inference-123 started on node g4dn-02 (after RBAC fix).

security-bot: For follow-up: we should add an automated test in infra-ci that runs `kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer -n gpu-pool` as part of the infra plan step. Also add a note to runbook: 'When refactoring RBAC, run local can-i tests and check audit sink for 403 spikes'.

morgan: Agreed. Also add a lint to deny new ClusterRoleBindings referencing wildcard subjects. We need to avoid reintroducing cluster-wide grants for deployment SAs.

alex: I'll include both the can-i check and a policyguard rule in the PR. Leaving this thread open until TF apply completes and audit sink shows no new 403s.

sasha: Thanks all — I’ll monitor the splunk alerts and post if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
